transcript.text: Every so often when I use the hob the electrics in the house go off. Not every time, maybe once a week. It's an induction hob, Hisense I think.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. First switch it off at the wall or cooker switch and let it cool completely. No—an induction hob should not intermittently take out the house electrics. Do not use it again until a qualified appliance/electrical engineer has checked it; repeatedly resetting the switch can mask a developing electrical fault. The more likely causes are an insulation fault in an induction coil or power module, then the hob’s supply cable/connection; moisture from a spill is another possibility.

claimsRejected.claim: A switch trips when the hob fault occurs.

candidates: Induction power module or coil insulation fault causing earth leakage (high)
Hob supply cable or connection fault (medium)
Moisture or spill-related tracking within the hob (low)

reading.symptom: house electrics go off intermittently when using the hob

plan: Safety: a supply trip hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Hisense.
The fault they reported is: "house electrics go off intermittently when using the hob". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
